'''R. Bruce King''' is emeritus professor at the [[University of Georgia]].<ref name="uga">{{Cite web |url=https://www.chem.uga.edu/directory/people/r-bruce-king |title=R Bruce King |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Dept. of Chemistry |publisher=University of Georgia |access-date=October 29, 2024}}</ref>  He has contributed to many areas of [[organometallic chemistry]], including synthesis, spectroscopy, and theory.  He is the author and editor of several monographs and book series.<ref>King, R. B. Organometallic Syntheses. Volume 1 Transition-Metal Compounds; Academic Press: New York, 1965. {{ISBN|0444426078}}.</ref>  
  
[[Image:Fe2 SMe 2 CO 6.svg|166px|thumb|Structure of [[Methylthioirontricarbonyl dimer|Fe<sub>2</sub>(SCH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>(CO)<sub>6</sub>]], isomers of which King separated and characterized.<ref>{{cite journal|first=R. B. |last=King|title=Organosulfur Derivatives of Metal Carbonyls. I. The Isolation of Two Isomeric Products in the Reaction of Triiron Dodecacarbonyl with Dimethyl Disulfide|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.|year=1962|volume=84|issue=12 |page=2460|doi=10.1021/ja00871a045|bibcode=1962JAChS..84.2460K }}</ref>]]

==Training and research interests==
He received his Ph.D. in 1961 under the direction of [[F. Gordon A. Stone]] at Harvard for research on [[organocobalt]] and [[organoiron compound]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Kaesz, H. D. |author2=King, R. B. |author3=Manuel, T. A. |author4=Nichols, L. D. |author5=Stone, F. G. A. |title=Chemistry of the metal carbonyls. V. The desulfurization of thiophene|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.|year=1960|volume=82|issue=17 |pages=4749–4750|doi=10.1021/ja01502a080|bibcode=1960JAChS..82.4749K }}</ref>  He subsequently conducted studies on synthetic organometallic chemistry at DuPont and then at the [[Mellon Institute]]. His endeavors led to the first examples of [[Diazonium compound|diazonium complexes]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=King, R. B.|title=Thirty Years of Organometallic Aryldiazenido Aryldiazo Derivatives|journal=J. Organomet. Chem.|year=1995|volume=500|issue=1–2 |page=187|doi=10.1016/0022-328X(95)00504-J }}</ref>  His contributions also include [[Organophosphorus compound|organophosphorus]] ligands.

==Recognition==
Among his accolades, King was recognized by the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|American Chemical Society]] Awards in [[ACS Award in Pure Chemistry|Pure Chemistry]] (1971) and in Inorganic Chemistry (1991).
